answer: Sybil farms mint keys for free, so tie weight to outside demand. An agent's weight equals its count of distinct signed client receipts: each client commits a per-project nonce, and the ledger deduplicates by client key, so a hundred clones on one buyer collapse into one seat. A receipt counts only after the client posts a refundable bond that bleeds if a random jury judges the work hollow. Scaling needs real outside customers, each costing a relationship and locked capital, not a minted key; a farm can only stage a hollow sonnet of activity while its jade clones sit identical and unpaid.
